results.title: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis of ...
results.content: The aim of this study is to systematically capture, synthesize, and evaluate current research trends related to Automated Multiple-Choice Question Generation as they emerge within the broader landscape of natural language processing (NLP) and large language model (LLM)-based educational and assessment research. To the best of our knowledge, this study represents the first systematic bibliometric analysis that examines Automated Multiple-Choice Question Generation research within the context of the broader LLM-driven educational assessment literature. The bibliometric analysis carried out for the period 2023–2025 includes 240 publications from 149 scientific journals, which demonstrates intense research activity in the field of automatic MCQ generation and, more generally, in the applications of artificial intelligence in education. The present study, by mapping this new phase of development (2023–2025), provides a holistic picture of the course of the field and contributes substantially to the understanding of contemporary research trends, thematic correlations, and future prospects in the field of automatic question generation through NLP and artificial intelligence technologies in education.

results.title: Guidance for the reporting of bibliometric analyses
results.content: For each eligible source, the following information was extracted: authors and year of publication; country of corresponding author; document objective; study design or source type; journal subject scope; whether a source gave special focus to non-bibliometric subjects; whether a document gave special focus to bibliometrics for use in hiring, promotion, or tenure; whether the reporting recommendations were evidence based (i.e., if sources adhered to EQUATOR’s “How to develop a reporting guideline” toolkit [EQUATOR, 2018c]); whether a document provided reporting examples by conducting a bibliometric analysis; the number of reporting recommendations mentioned; and whether conceptual frameworks were used to understand bibliometric analyses. Only one included source adhered to EQUATOR’s recommendations (EQUATOR, 2018c) by conducting a systematic literature review and a Delphi consensus process to create a reporting guideline for bibliometric analyses, referred to as BIBLIO (Montazeri et al., 2023).

results.title: How does artificial intelligence shape the productivity and ...
results.content: We investigate how Artificial Intelligence (AI) enhances the productivity and quality of research in business studies. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) addresses these issues by enhancing the speed and accuracy of data processing, allowing researchers to handle vast datasets and uncover meaningful insights more effectively [7:53–8.")]. This strategy was expected to provide a systematic review of the effects of AI on methods, research quality, and ethics in Business Studies, identifying 1760 papers. AI technologies, notably machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP), have significantly enhanced the quality of business research by enabling large-scale data processing and pattern recognition. Ethical concerns, including data privacy, intellectual property, and algorithmic bias, remain central to the responsible adoption of AI in business research [57:9–28. By integrating insights from Decision-Making Theory, Information Processing Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and maintaining a vigilant commitment to ethics, future AI applications in business research can propel innovation while upholding the values necessary for sustainable and responsible progress.
